sections.description: The Departure of Elijah and the Ministry of Elisha

sections.title: The Two Kingdoms
sections.description: Jehu's Dynasty, The Fall of the Northern Kingdom

events.title: Elijah Taken Up to Heaven
events.description: The prophet Elijah and his servant Elisha travel together from Gilgal through Bethel and Jericho to the Jordan. Elijah strikes the water with his cloak, and they cross over on dry ground. A chariot of fire with horses of fire separates them, and Elijah is taken up to heaven in a whirlwind.

events.title: Elisha Inherits Elijah's Spirit
events.description: Elisha picks up the cloak that fell from Elijah and strikes the water of the Jordan, which parts before him. The prophets in Jericho see this and recognize that the spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha. He purifies the water at Jericho and begins his prophetic ministry.

events.title: Elisha and the Widow's Oil
events.description: A prophet's widow is threatened by her creditors, who intend to take her two sons as slaves. Elisha tells her to gather empty jars from her neighbors and pour out the small amount of oil she has. The oil miraculously multiplies until all the jars are full, enabling her to sell it and pay off her debt.

events.title: Elisha and the Shunammite Woman
events.description: A wealthy woman in Shunem prepares a room for Elisha. He promises her a son, who is born the following year. When the boy later dies from sunstroke, Elisha lies over the child and prays to the Lord, and the boy is restored to life.

events.title: Naaman Healed of Leprosy
events.description: Naaman, the commander of the army of Aram, suffers from leprosy. An Israelite slave girl tells about the prophet Elisha. Naaman travels to Israel and is told to bathe seven times in the Jordan. After reluctantly obeying, he is healed. He confesses that there is no God except in Israel.

events.title: Elisha Makes the Axe Head Float
events.description: While building a new dwelling place for the sons of the prophets, a borrowed axe head falls into the Jordan. Elisha throws a stick into the water, and the heavy iron axe head floats to the surface.

events.title: The Siege of Samaria by Aram
events.description: Ben-Hadad of Aram besieges Samaria, causing a terrible famine. Elisha prophesies that there will be an abundance of food the next day. Four men with leprosy discover that the Arameans have fled in panic, and the city is saved.

events.title: Jehu Anointed as King
events.description: Elisha sends a prophetic apprentice to anoint Jehu, son of Jehoshaphat, as king over Israel. Jehu is commissioned to destroy the house of Ahab in revenge for the blood of the prophets and the Lord's servants that Jezebel has killed.

events.title: Jehu Kills Joram and Jezebel
events.description: Jehu rides to Jezreel and shoots King Joram of Israel with an arrow that pierces his heart. Jezebel is thrown from a window by her own courtiers and trampled by horses. Jehu's bloody revolution completely wipes out Ahab's dynasty.

events.title: Jehu Wipes Out the House of Ahab and Baal Worship
events.description: Jehu kills all seventy sons of Ahab in Samaria and all his nobles. He tricks the worshipers of Baal into the temple of Baal and kills them all. The pillar of Baal and the temple are torn down. But Jehu does not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam with the golden calves.

events.title: Athaliah and Joash
events.description: Queen mother Athaliah seizes power in Judah and kills the entire royal family. But the young prince Joash is hidden in the temple for six years by the priest Jehoiada and his wife. In the seventh year, Jehoiada crowns Joash as king, and Athaliah is executed.

events.title: Joash Repairs the Temple
events.description: King Joash orders that the money collected at the temple be used to repair the building. The priests neglect the work, so Joash establishes a new system with a collection chest at the entrance. The temple is thoroughly restored.

events.title: The Death of Elisha
events.description: Elisha becomes ill and lies near death. King Joash of Israel visits him weeping. Elisha tells the king to shoot an arrow and strike the ground with it as a sign of victory over Aram, but the king strikes only three times. After Elisha's death, a dead man is placed in his tomb, and the man comes back to life when he touches Elisha's bones.

events.title: The Fall of Samaria and the End of the Northern Kingdom
events.description: After repeated disobedience and idolatry, Shalmaneser of Assyria besieges Samaria for three years. The city falls in 722 BC, and the people of the northern kingdom are taken into exile to Assyria. The king of Assyria settles foreign peoples in Samaria, who mix their worship with the worship of the Lord.

events.title: Hezekiah becomes king and carries out reforms
events.description: Hezekiah becomes king over Judah and does what is right in the eyes of the Lord. He removes the high places, breaks down the sacred pillars, cuts down the Asherah poles, and shatters the bronze serpent that Moses had made, because the Israelites had begun to worship it.

events.title: Sennacherib's siege of Jerusalem
events.description: The Assyrian king Sennacherib invades Judah and besieges Jerusalem. His envoys mock the God of Israel and threaten the people. Hezekiah prays in the temple, and the prophet Isaiah brings God's answer. During the night, the angel of the Lord strikes down 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp. Sennacherib withdraws and is later killed by his own sons.

events.title: Hezekiah's illness and healing
events.description: Hezekiah becomes mortally ill. The prophet Isaiah tells him that he will die. Hezekiah turns his face to the wall and weeps, praying to the Lord. God hears his prayer and adds fifteen years to his life. As a sign, God causes the shadow to move ten steps backward on the sundial of Ahaz.

events.title: Manasseh's Evil Reign
events.description: Manasseh becomes king at twelve years old and reigns for fifty-five years. He restores the high places, builds altars to Baal, sets up an Asherah pole in the temple, sacrifices his own son in the fire, practices sorcery and divination. He sheds so much innocent blood that Jerusalem is filled from one end to the other.

events.title: The Book of the Law Found in the Temple
events.description: During repairs to the temple, the high priest Hilkiah finds the Book of the Law. When it is read to King Josiah, he tears his clothes in despair over the people's disobedience. The prophetess Huldah confirms that God's judgment will come upon Judah, but not during Josiah's lifetime because his heart was humble.

events.title: Josiah's Reforms
events.description: Josiah gathers all the people and reads the Book of the Covenant to them. He removes all idols from the temple, dismisses idolatrous priests, tears down the high places, destroys Topheth in the Valley of Hinnom, and thoroughly cleanses the land. He celebrates the greatest Passover since the days of the judges.

events.title: Josiah's Death at Megiddo
events.description: Pharaoh Neco of Egypt marches north to help the Assyrian king. King Josiah goes out to meet him in battle at Megiddo but is killed. His servants bring his body back to Jerusalem, and all Judah mourns the death of this righteous king.

events.title: Nebuchadnezzar's First Siege
events.description: Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon decides to subdue Judah. King Jehoiakim becomes his vassal for three years but then rebels. The Lord sends Chaldean, Aramean, Moabite, and Ammonite forces against Judah because of Manasseh's sins.

events.title: Jehoiachin Exiled to Babylon
events.description: The young king Jehoiachin reigns for only three months before Nebuchadnezzar's army besieges Jerusalem. Jehoiachin surrenders and is taken to Babylon along with his mother, servants, officials, and courtiers. Ten thousand captives are exiled, including all craftsmen and smiths. Only the poorest people of the land remain. Nebuchadnezzar installs Zedekiah as a vassal king.

events.title: The Fall and Destruction of Jerusalem
events.description: After Zedekiah rebels, Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem for a year and a half. Famine becomes desperate. The city wall is breached, and Zedekiah flees but is captured at Jericho. His sons are killed before his eyes, he is blinded, and taken to Babylon. Nebuzaradan burns the temple, the king's palace, and all important houses. The city walls are torn down.

events.title: Gedaliah as Governor
events.description: Nebuchadnezzar appoints Gedaliah as governor over those remaining in Judah. Gedaliah urges the people to serve the king of Babylon and live in peace. But Ishmael from the royal line kills Gedaliah and his men. The rest of the people flee in fear to Egypt, leaving the land desolate.
